sections.h2: Who values and who bills property in Rutherford County?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work here: the Property Assessor sets values and the County Trustee sends the bills. Both are based in Murfreesboro, which sits at the geographic center of Tennessee, and the Trustee also keeps an office in Smyrna.

  • Property Assessor: 615-898-7750, with an online parcel search at rcpatn.com and a drop box outside the County Office Building at 319 N. Maple St.
  • County Trustee (Teb Batey): Murfreesboro 615-893-5210, Smyrna and Eagleville 615-898-7705. La Vergne collects its own city tax at 615-793-3388.
  • Register of Deeds (Heather Dawbarn): records the deeds that tell the Assessor who the new owner is.

Rutherford is the fifth most populous county in Tennessee, and the online payment portal and the phone line are listed alongside the counters.

sections.h2: How fast is the Rutherford County housing market growing?
sections.html:
Growth has been quick. An estimated 386,352 people lived here on July 1, 2025, compared with 341,482 at the April 2020 base, a rise of 13.1 percent across 619.27 square miles of land.

For 2020 to 2024 the median owned home was worth $382,600 and median household income was $85,470. Owners live in 64.8 percent of homes, rent at the median is $1,502, builders pulled 3,169 permits in 2025, and the typical commute is 28.1 minutes.

Employers shape the map. Nissan in Smyrna and La Vergne is listed at about 8,000 workers, Middle Tennessee State University and an Amazon fulfillment center anchor Murfreesboro, and Stones River National Battlefield preserves the 1862 to 1863 Civil War battle site. The county was formed in 1803 from parts of Davidson, Williamson and Wilson counties and named for Revolutionary War general Griffith Rutherford. Incorporated places are Murfreesboro, La Vergne and Eagleville, plus the Town of Smyrna.

sections.h2: What rate do Rutherford County owners pay per $100?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ lists a 2025 county levy of $1.8762 on each $100 of assessed value. Two municipalities add their own levy: Smyrna at $0.5257 and Eagleville at $0.4051.

Smyrna and Eagleville owners get one combined bill because the Trustee has collected for Smyrna since October 2017 and for Eagleville since October 2019. Murfreesboro and La Vergne bill separately, with their own tax pages linked from the Trustee site. A house inside either of those cities has two collectors, so request both payoff figures before closing.

Levies can change from year to year, so rely on the number printed on your current bill.

sections.h2: What is the Rutherford County billing schedule?
sections.html:
Bills come due the first Monday in October. Payment is interest free through the last day of February, and there is no discount for paying early.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Rutherford County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Options include the Trustee's online portal, the phone line, the counters and the mail. Phone payments run through 1-888-546-4299 and need a seven digit receipt number, with leading zeros if it is shorter.

  • In person: cash, check, cards, money orders and cashier's checks at both office locations. Make checks payable to Rutherford County Trustee.
  • Regular mail: PO Box 1316, Murfreesboro, TN 37133.
  • Overnight delivery: Rutherford County Trustee, Historic Courthouse, Room 102, Murfreesboro, TN 37130.
  • With every payment: include a daytime phone number and the receipt or account number.

Mortgage servicers receive tax data on request, so the paper bill is for your information if the lender pays through escrow.

sections.h2: Who is responsible for the tax bill when a Rutherford County house sells?
sections.html:
New owners are told to read the closing statement or ask the title company who owes what, and the Trustee warns that unpaid taxes keep accruing against the property. The annual bill covers January 1 through December 31.

Business owners get a similar rule. A business that was operating on January 1 owes personal property tax for the full year, even if it closed before December 31. Call the County Clerk at 615-898-7800 and the Assessor at 615-898-7750 if a business has shut down.

Short term rental owners face a separate filing. The Assessor's notice set September 1, 2026 as the last day for a questionnaire and affidavit covering the 2027 tax year. That date is behind us, so call the office about the next cycle if the house is rented by the night.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Rutherford County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, in three steps: an Assessor review, the local equalization board, then the State Board of Equalization. The state appeals handbook says county boards generally begin hearings on June 1.

A state filing must arrive by August 1 or within 45 days after the local board's notice, whichever is later (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). Assessments reflect the situation on January 1. The Assessor's site features a presentation on property values and revaluation for 2022, which it labels a reappraisal year, so check that page for the current cycle.

sections.h2: What will the Rutherford register charge to file my deed?
sections.html:
Deeds are billed at $5.00 a page, $10.00 minimum, plus a $2.00 computer fund fee, and the state conveyance tax is $3.70 for each $1,000. A $1.00 fee is collected only when that state tax is paid. The fee list cites T.C.A. 8-21-1001.

On a house that sells for $350,000, the conveyance tax alone works out to $1,295. The Register's office says it is not licensed and bonded to perform title searches and never guarantees that a property is free and clear, so a title company handles that step. The office also offers a MyLandAlert notice service for early warning of land fraud on your parcel.

sections.h2: Which relief programs does Rutherford County offer?
sections.html:
The Trustee's site describes two programs, a Senior Tax Freeze and veterans relief for disabled veterans and surviving spouses, and both are limited to a primary residence.

  • Senior Tax Freeze: homeowners 65 and older can freeze the tax at the amount for the year they qualify, up to five acres. The income limit is recalculated yearly and you must reapply annually. Remodeling raises the frozen amount, and a sale or loss of eligibility returns the house to current value and rate.
  • Veterans relief: the benefit is figured on the first $175,000 of market value. The deadline to apply is 35 days after the jurisdiction's delinquency date, and taxes must be paid by then.

A surviving spouse must have been married to the veteran at death and must not have remarried.

faqs.q: What is Rutherford's 2025 property tax rate?
faqs.a: County level: $1.8762 per $100 of assessed value. Smyrna adds $0.5257, Eagleville adds $0.4051, and Murfreesboro and La Vergne collect their own city taxes.

faqs.q: When do Rutherford County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: After the last day of February. Taxes are due the first Monday in October, and from the delinquency date unpaid balances accrue 1.5 percent interest each month.

faqs.q: Does paying early earn a discount in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: No. The Trustee states that Rutherford County does not offer an early payment discount, so paying in October saves nothing compared with paying in February.

faqs.q: Who handles a value dispute in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: Call the Property Assessor at 615-898-7750 first. If the county board does not settle it, the State Board of Equalization is next, on the August 1 or 45 day deadline.

faqs.q: Can Rutherford County seniors freeze their tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners 65 and older on a primary residence, up to five acres, with a new application each year. Call the Trustee at 615-898-7705 for the current income limit.
